name: Paraty and Ilha Grande
region: Costa Verde, Rio de Janeiro State
tagline: A perfectly preserved colonial port of whitewashed houses and cobbled streets, and a car-free island of rainforest and beaches, on a green coast between Rio and São Paulo.
highlight: A schooner cruise around the bay, with swims off deserted islands and cachaça in hand.
shortDescription: A UNESCO-listed colonial town on a bay, with cobbled streets, cachaça distilleries and schooner trips, plus the traffic-free island of Ilha Grande with jungle trails and beaches.
metaDescription: A Paraty and Ilha Grande travel guide: the historic centre, bay boat trips, cachaça, Trindade beaches, Ilha Grande's Lopes Mendes beach, hiking, the FLIP festival, how to get there from Rio and a three-day plan.
nearestAirport: Rio Galeão (GIG) or São Paulo Guarulhos (GRU); no commercial airport at Paraty
knownFor: Colonial old town, beaches, boat trips, cachaça, Ilha Grande's trails
goodFor: Colonial architecture, islands, beaches, hiking, relaxing

image.alt: The whitewashed colonial buildings and cobbled streets of the historic centre of Paraty

intro: Paraty, on Brazil's Costa Verde, or Green Coast, was founded in the 17th century, and it became a major port for shipping gold from Minas Gerais to Portugal along the Estrada Real. When the gold route moved to Rio, Paraty faded, and its centre was left nearly untouched, a perfectly preserved colonial town of whitewashed houses with brightly painted doors, cobbled streets and old churches. UNESCO inscribed it in 2019, together with Ilha Grande, for its culture and biodiversity.

The streets of the centre are closed to cars, and were designed with a slope and stones that allow the sea to flush them at high tide. Restaurants, galleries and pousadas fill the old houses, and the waterfront is busy with boats. The surrounding hills produce cachaça, the sugarcane spirit, and Paraty is famous for its distilleries.

Offshore, the bay is dotted with islands, and schooner trips are a highlight. Just to the east, Ilha Grande, a large island with no cars, has rainforest trails, empty beaches and a former prison. Together, they make an ideal escape from Rio and São Paulo, and are best visited from March to October, avoiding the busy summer weeks.

whyVisit.intro: Paraty and Ilha Grande combine colonial charm with tropical scenery, a short trip from Rio.

points.title: A preserved colonial centre
points.text: Walk through streets, churches and squares that look much as they did in the 18th century.

points.title: Boat trips
points.text: Schooners take you to islands and beaches in the bay.

points.title: Ilha Grande
points.text: A car-free island of jungle, trails and beaches.

points.title: Culture and festivals
points.text: Literary festival, music and art galleries.

attractionsIntro: Give Paraty a day, and Ilha Grande a night or two.

attractions.name: The historic centre
attractions.text: A grid of cobbled streets with whitewashed colonial houses, brightly painted doors, churches such as Santa Rita and Nossa Senhora dos Remédios, and small museums.
attractions.tip: Explore in the morning, before the crowds and the heat.

attractions.name: Schooner trips in Paraty Bay
attractions.text: Traditional wooden boats take you to islands and beaches, with swimming, snorkelling and lunch on board.
attractions.tip: Book a half- or full-day trip.

attractions.name: Cachaça distilleries
attractions.text: Small distilleries around Paraty produce artisanal cachaça, and offer tours and tastings.

attractions.name: Trindade
attractions.text: A fishing village and beaches about 30 km south of Paraty, with a natural rock pool, Cachadaço, and a relaxed atmosphere.

attractions.name: Ilha Grande and Lopes Mendes beach

image.alt: The long white sand of Lopes Mendes beach on Ilha Grande

attractions.text: A car-free island with a village, Abraão, and beaches including Lopes Mendes, a 3-km stretch of pale sand often ranked among the best in Brazil, reached by a trail or boat.
attractions.tip: Spend at least a night on the island.

attractions.name: Pico do Papagaio
attractions.text: A hike on Ilha Grande to a peak with views across the island and the sea.

thingsToDoIntro: Paraty and Ilha Grande are for slow days by the sea and on trails.

thingsToDo.title: Take a schooner trip
thingsToDo.text: Swim, snorkel and enjoy a seafood lunch on board.

thingsToDo.title: Taste local cachaça
thingsToDo.text: Try different aged and flavoured spirits.
thingsToDo.tip: Buy a bottle to take home.

thingsToDo.title: Hike on Ilha Grande
thingsToDo.text: Trails lead through Atlantic rainforest to beaches.

thingsToDo.title: Snorkel at Lagoa Azul
thingsToDo.text: A calm lagoon with clear water and fish.

thingsToDo.title: Attend the FLIP festival
thingsToDo.text: The Paraty International Literary Festival, held in the town in the middle of the year, attracts writers and readers from around the world.

thingsToDo.title: Kayak the bay
thingsToDo.text: Paddle through mangroves and quiet coves.

foodIntro: Paraty's food is coastal Brazilian, with fish, shrimp and local specialities.

foods.name: Fish and seafood moqueca
foods.text: Fish and shrimp stews in coconut milk.

foods.name: Azul-marinho
foods.text: A local dish of fish stewed with unripe banana, giving a bluish tint.

foods.name: Cachaça
foods.text: Aged and flavoured spirits, including cachaça with honey and cinnamon (gabriela).

accommodation.intro: Stay in a pousada in the historic centre, or on Ilha Grande.

gettingThere.intro: Paraty is on the coast road between Rio and São Paulo.

options.text: About 4 to 4.5 hours along the Costa Verde, with several daily services.

options.mode: Bus or car from São Paulo
options.detail: Take a bus or rent a car.

options.text: Boats and ferries link Paraty and Angra dos Reis with Abraão.

gettingAround.intro: The centre is on foot, and the coast is by bus and boat.

options.text: To the bay's islands and Ilha Grande.

bestTime.headline: April–October
bestTime.summary: Paraty has a humid tropical climate, with rain all year and a wetter summer.

seasons.text: Hot, humid, rainy and crowded, with high prices.
Warm, less crowded and often clear.
Mild and drier, with clear days.

bestTime.avoid: Christmas to Carnival, when the town is crowded and expensive.

itinerary.title: Three days in Paraty and Ilha Grande
itinerary.intro: The old town, the bay and the island.

tipsIntro: A few tips make the trip easier.
tips: Book accommodation early for holidays and festivals.
Wear comfortable shoes for the cobbles.
Bring insect repellent, sunscreen and a rain jacket.
Take cash for small stalls and boats.
Check tides and the weather for boat trips.
Take ferries early in the morning.
Do not leave belongings unattended on the beach.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Paraty?
faq.a: Two to three days, and more if you include Ilha Grande.

faq.q: Can I visit as a day trip from Rio?
faq.a: It is a long day. A night or two is better.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit?

faq.a: Yes, for beaches, hiking and a relaxed atmosphere. Allow at least one night.
Generally, yes. It is a small, relaxed town.

faq.q: Can I drive in the centre?
faq.a: No, the historic centre is closed to cars.
